title: Pod operations
description: What an agent or person can do in a pod, as plain HTTP/JSON operations. This list is the contract. MCP (at /mcp) and the CLI are adapters generated from it, so no capability exists only in one adapter. The actor always comes from the bearer token; no operation takes an actor argument. Errors return common.json ErrorBody.
x-rules: A GET operation takes its input as query parameters; any other method takes it as a JSON body.
{podId} in a path is the pod; with a run token it must be the run's pod, or the call gets forbidden. Any other {name} in a path is the input field of that name, and is not repeated in the body.
The MCP adapter exposes each operation as one tool named x-mcp-prefix plus the operation name, with the same input and output. The CLI exposes each as a subcommand. Neither adds behaviour.
Every operation a run token makes is recorded as a ToolCallRecord with source pod.

task_release may be called by the run that holds the claim, by the owner of the claiming agent (the user whose computer registered it), or by a pod owner; anyone else gets forbidden. Releasing an unclaimed task changes nothing and returns the task.
A claim released by a person is not restored: if that run later operates on the task it gets forbidden. The restore rule in ADR 0002 applies only to lease expiry.

run_stop may be called only by a person: the owner of the run's agent or a pod owner; anyone else gets forbidden. A run token cannot stop a run. Stopping a run that already ended returns its outcome unchanged.

run_stop acts at once and does not wait for the daemon: it revokes the run token (the run's next call gets unauthorized), releases the run's claims without restore, ends the run as cancelled and sends the run.stop event to the hosting computer. It works while that computer is offline. The pod emits task.updated and claim.released with cause stopped for each released claim; no separate audit store exists.
connector_call names exactly one of connectionId or vendor; vendor names the pod's one connection to that vendor. Neither, both, or a vendor with several connections gets invalid_input.

connector_call is decided by the grant of the run's agent on the connection and by the operation's class in the pinned catalogue. An operation not in the pin gets not_found. No grant, or a write with only a read grant, gets forbidden.

A read with a read or write-with-confirm grant calls the upstream once and returns its result (state done). A write with write-with-confirm calls nothing: it is parked, the agent posts an ask (options a approve, b reject) whose body holds the exact arguments, and the call returns state parked with the decisionId.

Only a pod owner rules on that ask; another member's ruling is refused forbidden and leaves it open. A ruling of a releases exactly one upstream call with the parked arguments; the parked call is marked consumed in the transaction that records the ruling, so no second ruling, retry or race can release another. A ruling of b releases nothing.
A parked write expires 24 hours after it was parked: its decision becomes expired, a later ruling gets gone, and nothing is released.
Every connector call that names an existing connection writes a ConnectorReceipt, stamped by the server. An agent can read receipts and never write one.
The connection's credential never appears in any operation's output, any error, any receipt or any ask: an upstream error that echoes it has it removed.

x-operations.name: whoami
x-operations.description: Who you are in this pod: your agent identity, the pod, your current run and the task it's for, if any.

x-operations.name: read
x-operations.description: Read the pod: message headlines and tasks since a sequence number. Bodies are left out unless withBody is true.

x-operations.name: task_list
x-operations.description: List the pod's tasks, optionally filtered by status.

x-operations.name: task_claim
x-operations.description: Claim a task before working on it. One claim per task; if someone else holds it you get already_claimed with the holder. The claim renews while its run is alive (any operation on the run token, or the hosting daemon's heartbeat); see ADR 0002.

x-operations.name: task_update
x-operations.description: Set a task's status. Use done only when the task's work is finished.

x-operations.name: evidence
x-operations.description: The stamped tool calls on a run: what the pod and the daemon saw it do. Cite their ids in an ask's context; you can read these but never write them.

x-operations.name: task_release
x-operations.description: Drop a task's claim. The run that holds it, the owner of the claiming agent or a pod owner may call it. A run whose claim a person released cannot take it back; see ADR 0002 Recourse.

x-operations.name: run_stop
x-operations.description: Stop a run now: revoke its token, release its claims and end it as cancelled. The agent's owner or a pod owner may call it; it works when the computer is offline. See ADR 0002 Recourse.

x-operations.name: post
x-operations.description: Post to the pod. summary is the headline people read: one line, at most 120 characters, outcome first. Use kind ask with needs, 2 to 5 options and a context when a person must decide: every claim in the context cites the tool calls or messages it comes from (see evidence). progress and fyi posts never notify anyone. The receipt is added by the pod; don't write one.

x-operations.name: connector_list
x-operations.description: The pod's connections and the operations you may call on each: the pinned catalogue filtered by your agent's grant, never the live upstream list. No credential is ever shown.

x-operations.name: connector_call
x-operations.description: Call one pinned operation on a pod connection; the pod holds the credential. A read returns the upstream's result. A write parks as an ask showing its exact arguments, and runs once only if a pod owner approves.

x-operations.name: connector_receipts
x-operations.description: The server-stamped receipts of this pod's connector calls, newest first. Pass decisionId to read what became of a parked write after its ruling.

EvidenceInput.description: The run whose tool calls to list.

EvidenceOutput.description: The tool calls stamped on the run.

toolCalls.description: The stamped tool calls, at most 500.

WhoamiOutput.description: The pod, and for a run token your agent identity, your run and its task, if any. A user token gets the pod only.

agent.description: Present only for a run token: the agent this run belongs to.

runId.description: Present only for a run token: the caller's current run.

ReadInput.description: Which part of the pod to read.

sinceSeq.description: Read the messages and tasks since this sequence number.

withBody.description: Include message bodies. They are left out unless this is true.

ReadOutput.description: Messages and tasks, and the pod's current head sequence.

messages.description: Messages since sinceSeq. Bodies are left out unless withBody was true.

tasks.description: The tasks, filtered by status if one was given.

TaskClaimOutput.description: The claim's lease: the task and when the lease runs out. It renews while its run is alive (any operation on the run token, or the hosting daemon's heartbeat); see ADR 0002.

TaskUpdateStatus.description: The statuses task_update can set: every task status except open.

TaskUpdateInput.description: The new status for a task.

TaskReleaseInput.description: Which task to release, and an optional reason.

reason.description: Why the claim is being dropped, at most 160 characters.

RunStopInput.description: Which run to stop, and an optional reason.

reason.description: Why the run is being stopped, at most 160 characters.

RunStopOutput.description: The run and how it ended: cancelled, or its earlier outcome if it had already ended.

ConnectorVendor.description: An upstream service the pod can connect, each with a pinned catalogue in the repo.

ConnectorAccess.description: What a grant lets an agent do on a connection: read only, or also writes that each need a member's approval.

OperationClass.description: Whether a pinned operation only reads the upstream (read) or changes it (write).

ConnectorOperationName.description: An operation's name in the vendor's pinned catalogue, e.g. list_issues.

PinnedOperation.description: One operation of a pinned catalogue: its name, its class and the names of its arguments.

args.description: The argument names the pin records, in order.

ConnectorView.description: A connection as a caller sees it: its id, vendor and the pinned operations the caller may use. A run sees only what its agent's grant allows.

access.description: For a run token: its agent's grant on this connection.

operations.description: The pinned operations the caller may call.

ConnectorListOutput.description: The pod's connections. A run token sees only the connections its agent holds a grant on.

ConnectorCallInput.description: One call: which connection (by id or by vendor), which pinned operation, and its arguments.

args.description: The operation's arguments, as the upstream takes them. A write's are shown on its ask exactly as given.

ConnectorCallState.description: What became of a call: done (the upstream answered) or parked (a write waiting on a ruling).

ConnectorCallOutput.description: A done call carries the upstream's result; a parked one carries the decision a pod owner rules on.

decisionId.description: State parked: the decision of the ask that holds the write.

ConnectorOutcome.description: ok: a read answered. failed: the upstream failed the call. refused: the grant did not allow it. parked, released, rejected, expired: a write's way through its ask.

ConnectorReceipt.description: The server's record of one connector call. Stamped by the server from its own records; an agent can read it and never write it.

argsHash.description: SHA-256 of the arguments as canonical JSON (keys sorted), lower-case hex.

upstreamStatus.description: The HTTP status the upstream answered with, when it was called.

decisionId.description: A write: the decision of its ask.

approver.description: A released write: the member whose ruling released it.

result.description: A released write: the upstream's result.

settledAt.description: When the call reached its outcome: at once for a read, at the ruling or expiry for a write.

expiresAt.description: A parked write: when it expires unruled.

decisionId.description: Only the receipt of the write this decision holds.

PostOutput.description: The stored message's id and sequence number, and the decision id when the post is an ask.
